discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger turned ultracold atoms in optical lattices into programmable quantum simulators of strongly correlated matter. Their 2002 observation of the superfluid to Mott insulator transition showed that a Hubbard model could be realised with full control over interactions, dimensionality and filling. Esslinger then brought fermionic atoms into lattices, reaching the fermionic Mott regime and engineering artificial gauge fields and topological band structures. Greiner and Bloch developed quantum gas microscopes with single-site, single-atom resolution, allowing direct imaging of antiferromagnetic correlations, entanglement growth, many-body localisation and string order. These experiments established analogue quantum simulation as a new field: they answer questions about quantum many-body systems that classical computers cannot address, and they now serve as benchmarks for theory across condensed matter, statistical physics and quantum information. Their work turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into a working laboratory tool.
